name: SubstrateMap
description: Renders a single substrate: a substrate outline (from an explicit binding, an outline preset, or demo data) with items and labels overlaid in the data frame, colored by status. The data frame is placed relative to the substrate frame by origin anchor, offset, rotation and y-axis direction, and the whole construct is view-rotated. Clicking an element raises onItemSelected and exposes the selection via the Selected* attributes. Extends the abstract SubstrateMapBase (shell) and draws through the shared SubstrateMapEngine.

dependencyFiles.name: ../../Helpers/SubstrateMapEngine/SpatialFilter.js
dependencyFiles.description: SubstrateMapEngine spatial filters: the median over palette indices, and the repaint that turns a filtered index array back into pixels. Imports Engine for the empty-index marker and the buffer type.

dependencyFiles.name: ../../Helpers/SubstrateMapEngine/BinPalette.js
dependencyFiles.description: SubstrateMapEngine categorical fallback: the palette for bin codes that carry neither a StatusColorMapping entry nor a BinQuality. Imports Oklch and BinSeverity, both leaves; deliberately NOT imported by Engine.js.

dependencyFiles.name: ../../Helpers/SubstrateMapEngine/BinSeverity.js
dependencyFiles.description: SubstrateMapEngine severity ladder: the declared total order over bins, the BinQuality vocabulary and the two table builders. Served and preloaded here; it imports nothing and Engine.js imports it.

dependencyFiles.name: ../../Helpers/SubstrateMapEngine/E142.js
dependencyFiles.description: SubstrateMapEngine E142 domain module (types, placement, coordinate mapping). Registered so the project webserver serves and preloads it; the ES module cache guarantees a single evaluation across the controls that import it.

dependencyFiles.name: ../../Helpers/SubstrateMapEngine/E142Bins.js
dependencyFiles.description: SubstrateMapEngine E142 bin-payload decoder. Served and preloaded here; pulled through the module graph by E142Xml.js / E142Grid.js.

dependencyFiles.name: ../../Helpers/SubstrateMapEngine/E142Xml.js
dependencyFiles.description: SubstrateMapEngine E142.1 MapData XML parser. Served and preloaded here; imported by SubstrateMap.js for the E142MapData path.

dependencyFiles.name: ../../Helpers/SubstrateMapEngine/E142Grid.js
dependencyFiles.description: SubstrateMapEngine GridData normalizer. Served and preloaded here; imported by SubstrateMap.js for the GridData path.

dependencyFiles.name: ../../Helpers/SubstrateMapEngine/E142Item.js
dependencyFiles.description: SubstrateMapEngine E142.4 (Stream-21) item decoder. Served and preloaded here; imported by SubstrateMap.js for the E142TransferData path (bytes -> encoding sniff -> the E142Xml pipeline).

dependencyFiles.name: SubstrateMap.js
dependencyFiles.description: Contains all the main logic as ES module. Pulls SubstrateMapBase.js, Engine.js and the E142 domain modules (E142.js, E142Bins.js, E142Xml.js, E142Grid.js, E142Item.js) through the module graph in the correct order.

attributeCategories.name: Data
attributeCategories.description: Item layout, status, color mapping, labels and the substrate outline, typically supplied by MES / database / recipe.

attributeCategories.name: Origin
attributeCategories.description: Placement of the data frame relative to the substrate frame: anchor, offset, rotation and y-axis direction.

attributeCategories.name: View
attributeCategories.description: View-level transform of the whole construct (map rotation).

attributeCategories.name: Common
attributeCategories.description: Visual options: demo items, labels and the substrate identity position.

attributeCategories.name: Selection
attributeCategories.description: Selection (read-only). Selection mode and the read-only outputs describing the interacted element.

attributeCategories.name: SEMI E142
attributeCategories.description: SEMI E142 substrate map ingestion: the three mutually-exclusive map inputs (E142.1 MapData XML, the E142.4 Stream-21 transfer payload, and compact GridData JSON), their overlay / fallback / orientation modifiers, and the read-only map identity and error outputs.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-substrate-id
attributes.description: Identifier of the substrate, shown in the identity area. Unset (null) hides the identity area.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-substrate-identity-position
attributes.description: Where the substrate identity (SubstrateId) is shown relative to the map: 'above', 'below' or 'none'.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-show-demo-items
attributes.description: Draws a sample wafer of about 180 dies when no real ITEMS are bound. Useful at design time, and the empty state of the control. What suppresses it is real items - not a bound document that produced none, and not an outline. With an Outline or an OutlinePreset bound the demo is SCALED INTO it and centered, so a view that binds both gets both: the outline is the substrate and the demo fills it. The die count is the same at every size; the dies get smaller. Without an outline the demo draws its own 300 mm notch wafer, exactly as it always has. Set it to false to draw nothing at all when there is no data.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-show-labels
attributes.description: Toggle the labels drawn over the substrate.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-items
attributes.description: Item layout for the substrate: id, optional name/layer/orientation/status, opaque user_data and one or more geometries per item, authored in the DATA frame (+y per YAxisDirection). Colored by status via StatusColorMapping. Null draws no items (unless demo items are enabled).

attributes.name: data-tchmi-item-status-assignments
attributes.description: Per-item status overrides: [{ item_id, status }]. Each entry overrides the status embedded in the matching item and is mapped to a color via StatusColorMapping.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-status-color-mapping
attributes.description: Maps each status / bin string to a CSS color. A status with no entry falls back to the theme's unknown-status color.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-bin-quality-aliases
attributes.description: Maps an author-defined BinQuality token onto 'pass' or 'fail'. E142 reserves only 'Pass' and 'Fail' and leaves every other value to the application, so a document saying 'Reject', 'Good' or 'Schlecht' is legal and this control cannot interpret it: the bin draws in the unknown color and E142_BIN_QUALITY_UNMAPPED names the token and the bin code. Bind e.g. {"Reject": "fail"} and it resolves. Keys are case-insensitive and trimmed. Unset (null) leaves only the two reserved values recognized.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-bin-severity-priority
attributes.description: Bin codes in severity order, MOST SEVERE FIRST. The severity ladder knows pass, fail and unknown and nothing finer; this is where you say that Scrap is worse than Chipping. A code whose BinQuality resolves to pass is NEVER promoted and E142_BIN_SEVERITY_PRIORITY_IGNORED says so - promoting it could let a tile holding one passing and one failing die reduce to the passing bin. A code absent from the bound map is reported with E142_BIN_SEVERITY_PRIORITY_UNUSED and ignored. Unset (null) leaves the ladder alone.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-labels
attributes.description: Text labels drawn over the substrate, authored in the DATA frame (+y per YAxisDirection). Each label is a box (center, size, unit/prefix) whose text is drawn upright and clipped to the box.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-outline
attributes.description: The substrate outline: a single closed shape authored in the SUBSTRATE frame (+y up, origin at the substrate center), filled with the body color and stroked with the edge color. Its bounding box defines the fit box and the origin anchors. Takes precedence over OutlinePreset and the demo outline.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-outline-preset
attributes.description: Built-in SEMI substrate outline selected by key (e.g. 'si-6in-p100', 'si-12in', 'solar-m10', 'glass-gen4'). 'none' (default) selects no preset. A bound Outline takes precedence over the preset, and the preset over the demo outline. Disc-flats presets honor SecondaryFlatDirection; disc-notch presets honor NotchExaggeration.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-secondary-flat-direction
attributes.description: Placement of the secondary flat relative to the primary for disc-flats presets: 'cw' or 'ccw' (as seen on screen). Ignored by single-flat, notch, pseudo-square and rectangle presets, and by a bound Outline.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-notch-exaggeration
attributes.description: Visual magnification of the true notch depth for disc-notch presets (1 = to scale). Clamped to >= 1. Affects disc-notch presets only; a bound Outline is never scaled.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-origin-location
attributes.description: Anchor point where the data frame (D) origin attaches on the outline's bounding box: 'center', 'top-left', 'bottom-left', 'top-right' or 'bottom-right'. 'top' is the +y edge and 'left' the -x edge of the bounding box (in the substrate frame, +y up). Places the DATA frame for Items and Labels only; the Outline is authored in the substrate frame and never moves. When no Outline is bound the anchor box is the items' combined bounding box. For round wafers the SEMI convention is to keep this at 'center'. An unrecognized value keeps the current anchor.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-origin-offset-x
attributes.description: Extra translation of the data origin added to the anchor, along the SUBSTRATE +x axis. Base unit meter, scaled by OriginOffsetPrefix. Expressed along the substrate axes (+y up) regardless of YAxisDirection. Moves the DATA frame (Items and Labels) only; the Outline never moves.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-origin-offset-y
attributes.description: Extra translation of the data origin added to the anchor, along the SUBSTRATE +y axis (up). Base unit meter, scaled by OriginOffsetPrefix. Expressed along the substrate axes (+y up) regardless of YAxisDirection. Moves the DATA frame (Items and Labels) only; the Outline never moves.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-origin-offset-prefix
attributes.description: Metric prefix scaling the meter-based OriginOffsetX / OriginOffsetY, one of 'yocto', 'zepto', 'atto', 'femto', 'pico', 'nano', 'micro', 'milli', 'centi', 'deci', 'none'. Default 'milli' (so the offsets read directly in millimeters). An unrecognized value keeps the current prefix.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-origin-rotation
attributes.description: Rotation of the data-frame axes about the data origin, in degrees, counter-clockwise-positive as seen in the substrate frame (and CCW on screen). Rotates the Item/Label ensemble about the anchor, not about the substrate center. Does not affect the Outline.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-y-axis-direction
attributes.description: Direction of the data-frame Y axis: 'up' (default) or 'down'. 'down' mirrors the data Y axis for vision systems whose +y grows downward; a CCW-positive Item orientation authored in that y-down frame then renders clockwise on screen (the correct physical behavior). The origin offsets stay along the substrate axes (+y up) either way, and the Outline is unaffected. An unrecognized value keeps the current direction.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-show-origin-marker
attributes.description: Draw a diagnostic marker at the data origin: a crosshair plus a +x and a +y data-axis stub, each with an arrowhead (the +y head is doubled so the two axes are told apart by shape, not color). Off by default. The marker is drawn under the full data matrix (W * D2S), so it shows the data origin's position, OriginRotation and YAxisDirection at once - in particular YAxisDirection 'down' flips the +y stub to point downward on screen, the true direction of the authored y axis. Screen-constant in size and stroke width and drawn in the selection color; purely visual - it is never hit-tested and cannot be selected.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-map-rotation
attributes.description: Rotates the whole construct - outline, items, labels and origin marker - about the substrate frame origin, in degrees, counter-clockwise-positive on screen; the drawing is re-fitted so nothing is clipped. Display-only: it never changes item coordinates or the Selected* outputs, and a click hits the same item at any rotation. The fit is conservative (a 45deg-rotated square gets about sqrt(2) more margin). Default 0 leaves the view unrotated.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-view-substrate-side
attributes.description: Which face of the substrate to render from. A VIEW transform, like MapRotation - it changes what you look at, not what the document means. 'follow-map' (default) applies NO mirror and draws the map as seen from the face it describes; 'TopSide' mirrors when the map's SubstrateSide is BottomSide; 'BottomSide' mirrors when the map's SubstrateSide is TopSide. The mirror runs about the vertical axis (E142-0225 Figure R2-17). The document's own SubstrateSide never triggers a mirror by itself - its coordinate consequences are already carried by OriginLocation and AxisDirection, so mirroring on it would double-flip a conforming map. The GridData path has no side field at all and takes the XSD default TopSide, so ViewSubstrateSide='BottomSide' mirrors a GridData map. An unrecognized value warns and falls back to follow-map.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-selection-mode
attributes.description: Selection behavior, one of 'single' or 'multi'. 'single' (default) keeps exact single-select sibling semantics; 'multi' toggles membership on click/tap, clears on a click of empty space, and adds shift+drag rubber-band selection on pointer devices.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-selected-item-id
attributes.description: Read-only. Id of the LAST interacted element; null after a clear.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-selected-item-status
attributes.description: Read-only. Status / bin string of the LAST interacted element; null after a clear.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-selected-item-name
attributes.description: Read-only. Name of the LAST interacted element; null after a clear.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-selected-item-user-data
attributes.description: Read-only. Opaque user_data of the LAST interacted item, passed through unchanged; null for grid cells and after a clear.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-selected-items
attributes.description: Read-only. The full current selection as typed entries { kind, item_id, status, name, user_data }; 'cell' entries additionally carry binQuality and the signed logical mapX / mapY. kind is 'item' or 'cell'; user_data is null for cells. Null when nothing is selected.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-map-data
attributes.description: SEMI E142.1 MapData XML document. Parsed and rendered as a bin grid. Mutually exclusive with E142TransferData and GridData - the most recently written non-null input wins. Unset (null) unbinds it. A parse / placement failure is reported in E142LastError and clears the grid.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-map-data-json
attributes.description: SEMI E142.1 MapData document in its JSON representation - the SAME document E142MapData carries, in a different encoding, parsed by the same code to the same model, so a map bound here renders identically to the same map bound as XML. Arrives as a typed symbol rather than an opaque string; a string is accepted too. Mutually exclusive with E142MapData, E142TransferData and GridData - the most recently written non-null input wins. Unset (null) unbinds it. A parse failure is reported in E142LastError and clears the grid.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-grid-data
attributes.description: Compact GridData v1 document (the PLC-friendly single-map JSON contract). Normalized and rendered as a bin grid through the same pipeline as E142MapData. Mutually exclusive with E142MapData and E142TransferData. Unset (null) unbinds it.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-transfer-data
attributes.description: SEMI E142.4 (Stream-21) reassembled item content, as raw bytes: a base64 string or an array of byte values (0..255). This is the fallback for SECS drivers that deliver UNDECODED bytes (a B:n item, or a charset-agnostic driver); if your stack decodes the Stream-21 item to a string, bind that to E142MapData instead and leave this unset. Bytes are decoded (BOM / XML-declaration encoding sniff, UTF-8 default) to text and rendered through the same pipeline as E142MapData. Stream-21 reassembly is the host stack's job; this is the consumer side of E142.4's item content only. No ITEMTYPE string is inspected. Mutually exclusive with E142MapData and GridData. Both inline inputs cap at a few MB of payload. Unset (null) unbinds it.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-substrate-id
attributes.description: Which SubstrateMap of the E142 document to render, by its SubstrateId. Unset (null) does not filter. Together with E142LayoutSpecifier this is a COMPLETE selector: SubstrateMapKey is an xs:key over (SubstrateType, SubstrateId, LayoutSpecifier), so in any schema-valid document at most one map matches. Re-resolves without re-parsing. Ignored by the GridData path. NOTE: map selection does not consult this yet.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-layout-specifier
attributes.description: Which SubstrateMap of the E142 document to render, by its LayoutSpecifier - the third field of SubstrateMapKey. Unset (null) does not filter. Give the specifier exactly as written in the document, including path separators ('Top/Devices', not 'Devices'). Re-resolves without re-parsing. Ignored by the GridData path. NOTE: map selection does not consult this yet.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-overlay-name
attributes.description: Which overlay of the E142 document to render, by MapName. Unset (null) selects the first renderable BinCodeMap overlay in document order. Re-resolves without re-parsing. Ignored by the GridData path (GridData has no overlays).

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-overlay-version
attributes.description: Which overlay of the E142 document to render, by MapVersion - the second half of the XSD OverlayKey (MapName, MapVersion), so one SubstrateMap may carry Sort/1 and Sort/2. Unset (null) does not filter by version. An EMPTY STRING is not the same as null: it selects the overlay whose MapVersion is empty, which is a real addressable overlay because @MapVersion defaults to "" and an overlay omitting the attribute has "" as its key value. Re-resolves without re-parsing. Ignored by the GridData path. NOTE: overlay selection does not consult this yet.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-overlays
attributes.description: Ordered list of E142 overlays to compose: one base plus any number of decorations. Each entry is { name, version?, role? }. The base owns the fill and the geometry; decorations contribute per-cell marks only, never fills. THE ORDER IS YOURS - OverlayKey is (MapName, MapVersion), a set rather than a sequence, so E142 declares no z-order. Omit role on every entry and the FIRST is the base. Omit version to match any version; the EMPTY STRING is different, and selects overlays that state no version (MapVersion's XSD default is ""). Null - the default - keeps the single-overlay behavior of E142OverlayName / E142OverlayVersion; binding both is reported and this list wins, because a map has one renderable overlay and cannot take two answers.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-device-data-overlay-name
attributes.description: Which DeviceDataMap overlay supplies the per-cell parameter readings reported by onItemSelected and SelectedItems, chosen by its MapName. Null (the default) takes the first overlay that carries device data. SEPARATE FROM E142OverlayName, which picks the RENDERABLE overlay: OverlayType is an xs:choice, so one overlay carries a BinCodeMap OR a DeviceDataMap, never both - a document that draws bin codes and reports parameters is using two overlays and needs two selectors. A name matching no DeviceDataMap overlay is reported and no readings are supplied; showing another overlay's values under the requested name would be worse than showing none. Values join to parameter names BY INDEX: E142 Table 19 requires the order of values to match the order of parameters, and the values carry no names of their own.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-align-to-reference-devices
attributes.description: Opt-in registration of the placement onto the overlay's ReferenceDevices. Off by default, so placement is unchanged unless explicitly enabled. XML path only - a GridData document carries no reference devices, and the attribute is ignored on that path. When on, the grid is shifted so the reference devices' model cell centers land on their stated Positions: a least-squares TRANSLATION over every reference device that carries a Position, which places a single reference device exactly. No rotation and no scale - SEMI E142 gives reference devices no rotation or scale attribute, so a translation is the only fit their data determines. Position is the offset of the device's center from the substrate's center along the map's own axes, so a rotated (Orientation) or mirrored (AxisDirection) map has those axes rotated and flipped with it. A Position without its own Units is read in the layout's DefaultUnits. Reference devices with no Position, or whose Coordinates fall outside the grid, are ignored for alignment. Changing this re-commits the current map.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-fallback-step-size-x
attributes.description: Fallback column pitch in millimeters for a layoutless map. Used only when BOTH X and Y are set; setting exactly one logs a warning and falls back to the nominal fit heuristic. Unset (null) leaves it unset.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-fallback-step-size-y
attributes.description: Fallback row pitch in millimeters for a layoutless map; see E142FallbackStepSizeX (both are required to take effect). Unset (null) leaves it unset.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-orientation-offset
attributes.description: Degrees added to the map's Orientation before placement, a clockwise-positive source angle. The zero reference is a notch at 6 o'clock at Orientation 0; set 180 for sources using the opposite convention. Default 0.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-e142-last-error
attributes.description: Read-only. Last map-ingestion error message (machine code plus detail), or null when the active map rendered cleanly or nothing is bound.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-map-substrate-id
attributes.description: Read-only. Substrate id carried by the active map, or null. Also drives the identity area when SubstrateId is unset.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-map-lot-id
attributes.description: Read-only. Lot id of the active map's substrate, or null when the source carried none.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-map-good-devices
attributes.description: Read-only. Good-device count of the active map's substrate, or null when the source carried none.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-map-carrier-type
attributes.description: Read-only. Carrier type of the active map's substrate (E142 Substrate/CarrierType, e.g. 'FOUP'), or null when the source carried none.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-map-carrier-id
attributes.description: Read-only. Carrier id of the active map's substrate (E142 Substrate/CarrierId, LotIdType maxLength 80 - not the 32 of SubstrateId), or null when the source carried none.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-map-slot-number
attributes.description: Read-only. Slot number of the active map's substrate (E142 Substrate/SlotNumber), or null when the source carried none. ZERO IS A VALUE: the element is xs:nonNegativeInteger, so slot 0 is a real slot and is distinct from null. Test against null, not truthiness.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-map-substrate-number
attributes.description: Read-only. Substrate number within the lot (E142 Substrate/SubstrateNumber), or null when the source carried none. Zero is a value, as for MapSlotNumber.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-map-alias-ids
attributes.description: Read-only. Alternate identifiers of the active map's substrate (E142 Substrate/AliasIds), as an array of {type, value}. NULL - not an empty array - when the source document carried no AliasIds element: E142 cannot express an empty alias list (AliasIdsType requires at least one AliasId), so publishing [] would invent a statement the document never made. @Type is an open vocabulary; @Value is MaterialIdType, maxLength 32.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-map-substrate-count
attributes.description: Read-only. How many SubstrateMap elements the bound E142 document contains, or null when no map is bound. A DOCUMENT fact, not a substrate fact: it survives a selection failure, so a view can say 'your filter matched none of 3' rather than just 'not found'. A count above 1 means E142SubstrateId and E142LayoutSpecifier decide which one is rendered; leaving them unset renders the first in document order and logs a warning listing every candidate.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-aggregation-factor
attributes.description: Read-only. Cells per device pixel by AREA in the frame last drawn, or null when no map is bound. The number a legend needs for '1 px = 6 dies'. It is an area count, not a linear one: 6 dies per pixel is about 2.4 dies across. Read from the composed device matrix, so it follows a resize, a rotation and any injected view transform without the document being re-parsed. Null also when the lattice is degenerate, where every cell would share one pixel.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-aggregation-mode
attributes.description: Read-only. Which reduction produced the frame last drawn, or null when no map is bound. 'None' means every cell covers at least one device pixel and is drawn in its own right. 'PointSample' means cells are smaller than a pixel and the renderer still paints one cell per pixel - other cells in that pixel are invisible and which one survives depends on subpixel phase. Pair it with AggregationFactor in a legend so an operator can tell a summary from a datum.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-aggregation-reducer
attributes.description: Which reduction an aggregated tile uses. 'Auto' (the default) MEASURES each frame's saturation - the fraction of painted pixels holding at least one failing die - and selects the reducer for the next frame, switching to FailFraction above 0.6 and back below 0.4. It measures rather than inferring from the aggregation factor, because at one factor the chance a pixel holds a failing die runs from 0.5 % to 100 % depending on the defect rate. 'MaxSeverity' never hides a lone defect; 'FailFraction' never floods a noisy wafer. Force one when the view must not change under the operator - a report screenshot, or a panel where a map is always read the same way.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-touch-target-size
attributes.description: The smallest area a tap should be able to select, in CSS pixels. Default 40. When dies are drawn smaller than this, a tap selects a GROUP of them rather than one; painting is unaffected and still runs at one device pixel per bucket. 0 turns grouping off and is the only value that does: every tap then selects one die and raises onItemSelected, as it did before grouping existed - zero is the absence of a target rather than a small one, so the floor does not apply to it. Every OTHER value below 24, a negative number included, is clamped and reported with E142_TOUCH_TARGET_CLAMPED - 24 is WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), where the enhanced criterion is 44 and the phone guidelines 44 to 48. A CSS pixel is a reference unit, not a physical one: devicePixelRatio is accounted for, but two industrial panels of very different physical size both report a ratio near 1 and the platform exposes no reliable physical size, so the author overrides per panel.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-view-transform
attributes.description: An affine transform as the six components [a, b, c, d, e, f], post-multiplied onto the world matrix. Null is identity. GEOMETRY ONLY: it moves, scales, rotates, shears or mirrors what is drawn and cannot express a per-cell value - for a measurement per die, carry it as an E142 overlay with the valueField role instead. Because it is post-multiplied, e and f are in MILLIMETERS of the substrate frame and scaling is anchored at the canvas center; read MapScale to convert from pixels. The hit test, the aggregation factor and the layer cache key all track it, because it is composed into the world matrix they already consume. A zero determinant is refused with E142_VIEW_TRANSFORM_DEGENERATE and identity is used.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-map-scale
attributes.description: Read-only. CSS pixels per millimeter in the frame last drawn, or null when nothing is drawn. The number an author needs to use ViewTransform, whose translation is in MILLIMETERS: millimeters = pixels / MapScale. It is the FIT scale and excludes the author's own transform, so it does not move as they zoom - otherwise converting a pointer delta would need the answer being computed.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-map-substrate-side
attributes.description: Read-only. The SubstrateSide of the map actually being rendered ('TopSide' or 'BottomSide'), or null when no map is bound. On the GridData path this is always 'TopSide': GridData has no side field, and the E142 XSD default for an absent SubstrateSide is TopSide - so the value is the contract's, not an invention. Compare with ViewSubstrateSide to know whether a mirror is being applied.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-spatial-filter
attributes.description: Which spatial filter runs over the aggregated tile, in SCREEN space, after the render and before the blit. None is the default and changes nothing. Median takes the most common PALETTE INDEX in the neighborhood, so the answer is always a real bin color; Min and Max are erosion and dilation over severity rank; Box and Gauss average a scalar field and give a density map rather than a bin map. Median, Min and Max require FieldView Bins; Box and Gauss require FailDensity or ValueField. An illegal pairing does not filter and reports E142_FILTER_NOT_APPLICABLE naming both values.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-spatial-filter-radius
attributes.description: Filter radius in DEVICE pixels, 0 to 8. Zero disables the filter as surely as SpatialFilter None does, and is the value to bind when an operator should be able to turn it off from a slider. In device pixels rather than millimeters because the filter runs on the rendered tile: the same radius covers more dies as you zoom out, which is the point - it is a screen-space indicator, not a measurement of the wafer.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-field-view
attributes.description: Which channel the tile shows. Bins is the categorical view and the default. FailDensity paints the fraction of failing dies per pixel; ValueField paints a bound relevance map. Both of the latter are scalar fields, and only they may be averaged by Box or Gauss.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-field-gamma
attributes.description: Gamma applied to a scalar field before it is colored, so that the low end of the ramp is not compressed into one indistinguishable band. Below 1 lifts small values and makes a light scattering of failures visible; above 1 suppresses them. Ignored when FieldView is Bins, because a categorical view has nothing to curve.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-highlight-from-severity
attributes.description: Keep the color of every bin at or above this severity rank; everything below drops to the lightness of its own color at chroma 0. Gray, not hidden: a hidden cell is indistinguishable from a null cell, and the difference between 'there is nothing here' and 'there is something here that does not concern you right now' is exactly the one an operator needs. null highlights nothing and is the default. Ranks come from BinSeverityPriority when one is bound; without it the ladder is the three-rank fallback - 1 pass, 2 unknown, 3 fail - so 3 is the common value and means 'show me the failures'.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-reference-grid-data
attributes.description: A second map to compare the bound one against - an incoming map before rework, a golden wafer, a previous test step. An ordinary SubstrateMapGridData, deliberately: a reference is a map, and inventing a second schema for it would mean two parsers to keep in step. Ignored entirely while ReferenceMode is Off, so binding one costs nothing until a mode is chosen.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-reference-mode
attributes.description: How ReferenceGridData is compared against the bound map. Off ignores it. Difference shows every cell whose bin differs. NewOnly shows only the cells that got WORSE, which is the question an operator asks after a rework step.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-map-timestamp
attributes.description: Identical to the SubstrateMapWidget and SubstrateMapBinChart attributes of the same name, so ONE SYMBOL can drive a map, a tile and a chart showing the same wafer. Shown beside the substrate id in the identity band. When the map was MEASURED, if you can supply it. Bind it and the tile labels its age 'measured'; leave it and the tile labels the age 'received' instead, which is when the payload arrived here. The two are different facts - a map that arrived a second ago may describe a wafer tested this morning - so the tile always says which one it is showing. AN E142 DOCUMENT CARRIES NO TIMESTAMP OF ITS OWN. The ITEMVERSION value the SEMI standard defines belongs to the Stream 21 message that transports the item, not to the map, so a control that only sees the document cannot know when it was made. Bind it from wherever your transport keeps it. Accepts the SEMI form YYYYMMDDhhmmsscc and ISO 8601; a value with no timezone is read as local time, because a tester writes the time on its own clock.

functions.name: toGridData
functions.description: Serializes the currently bound map back to a canonical GridData document. Round-trips: binding the result to the GridData attribute reproduces the same grid. Returns null when no map is bound - the function is only meaningful once one of E142MapData, E142TransferData or GridData has produced a grid. Pitch is the drawn placement's: physical (mm) when the source map carried a scale, nominal otherwise, so a scale-less source round-trips as nominal rather than acquiring a fabricated physical size. E142OrientationOffset is deliberately NOT folded into the emitted orientation: the offset reconciles a source-side convention for display, so the export carries the source map's own Orientation and stays faithful to the input.

functions.name: toE142Xml
functions.description: Serializes the currently bound map back to a SEMI E142.1 MapData XML string, in the urn:semi-org:xsd.E142-1.V0125.SubstrateMap namespace. Round-trips through the E142MapData attribute. Returns null when no map is bound - the function is only meaningful once one of E142MapData, E142TransferData or GridData has produced a grid. Pitch is the drawn placement's: physical (mm) when the source map carried a scale, nominal otherwise, so a scale-less source round-trips as nominal rather than acquiring a fabricated physical size. E142OrientationOffset is deliberately NOT folded into the emitted orientation: the offset reconciles a source-side convention for display, so the export carries the source map's own Orientation and stays faithful to the input.

functions.name: readBinStatistics
functions.description: Returns the whole bound lattice counted by bin code: { totalCells, nullCount, bins: [ { code, count, quality, severity, color } ] }. UNTRUNCATED, unlike the onGroupSelected histogram - that caps at ten because an event payload is O(K) in something the document controls and is rebuilt on every tap, and neither is true of a function asked for once per binding. A bar chart that hides the eleventh-largest code is worthless. sum(bins[].count) + nullCount === totalCells, exactly and always. bins is descending by count then by code, so two readings of the same map serialize identically and a chart's bars do not reorder themselves. quality is the token the DOCUMENT declared, verbatim, or null - severity already carries the resolution and the declared token is the only field that cannot be recovered from the others. color is the color the RENDER PATH paints for that code, resolved through the same call buildGridPaint makes with the scene's StatusColorMapping and BinQualityAliases - not the raw mapping value, because a chart built from that disagrees with the map for every code the mapping does not name. With nothing bound the answer is totalCells 0 and an empty list, never null: an empty chart is a state a chart can draw, and null is a state every caller has to branch on. There is deliberately no bindable attribute - anyone who needs these numbers in a back end has an MES that already has them, and a bindable output would recount the lattice on every scene change to feed a symbol nobody reads.

functions.name: readGroupMembers
functions.description: Returns the cell indices a group holds, as a Uint32Array, computed on demand. onGroupSelected hands the author a SUMMARY - counts, a truncated histogram, a severity - because a 12 900-cell group as a list of objects is about 1.5 MB built and serialized on every tap. This is the escape hatch for the tap that needs more: a drill-down popup, an export, a follow-up query. Cheap by default, complete when asked - nothing is retained between calls and nothing is precomputed. A typed array and not item objects, so asking for the members does not allocate the thing the descriptor exists to avoid. Pass an id from a SubstrateMapGroupSelection produced in the CURRENT view; after a pan or a resize the group it named no longer exists and the result is empty rather than wrong.

params.name: groupId
params.description: A group id from a SubstrateMapGroupSelection, of the form "gx,gy".

functions.name: readAge
functions.description: The age shown in the identity band: local time, timezone abbreviation, whether it came from a bound MapTimestamp or from the receive clock, and the age in seconds. Same shape the tile and the chart return.

events.name: onItemSelected
events.description: Raised on every selection interaction. Event data carries { itemId, status, name, userData, kind, selection }; a 'cell' interaction additionally carries { column, row, binCode, binQuality, mapX, mapY, deviceId, lid, fromSubstrateType, fromSubstrateId, fromX, fromY, fromLid, deviceData } where column/row are serialization indices and mapX/mapY are signed logical E142 map coordinates. The last interacted element is mirrored in the SelectedItem* attributes, the full set in SelectedItems. deviceId is the identifier of the DEVICE in the cell (from a DeviceIdMap overlay) and lid is the identifier of the LOCATION itself (E142 BinCode/@LID); E142 13.4 makes them distinct - the location identifier is still present when the device is removed. Both are null when the map supplies none. The five from* fields are the R2-3 TRACEABILITY PATH: where the device now in this cell came from, read out of a TransferMap overlay (E142 13.9 / R2-3; R2-3.2.2 describes the wafer -> tape-and-reel -> target chain). They are null together when no transfer covers the cell. fromX/fromY and fromLid are alternatives - each end of a transfer is addressed either by coordinate or by identifier, never both. deviceData is an array of { name, value } - the DeviceDataMap parameter readings for the cell, joined by index per Table 19, with value already rendered for display; null when there are none. SelectedItems carries the same entries plus the raw E138 PvValue.

arguments.description: The selection payload. See SubstrateMapItemSelection: the six always-present fields describe the LAST INTERACTED element, the cell fields are present only for kind "cell", and a payload with every value null and an empty selection is a CLEAR.

events.name: onGroupSelected
events.description: Raised instead of onItemSelected when dies are drawn smaller than TouchTargetSize, so a tap covers a GROUP of them. Event data is the group descriptor: { id, corners, cellCount, severity, bins, otherCount, otherBins, decorated }, where corners are the group quad's four LATTICE-space corners and bins is a histogram truncated to the ten most common codes with the rest in otherCount. The member cells are NOT in the payload - a 12 900-cell group as a list of objects is about 1.5 MB built on every tap; call readGroupMembers(id) for them. onItemSelected is not raised alongside this: a group has no item id, status or user data, and a handler expecting one die would receive a summary of thousands. Which event fires is decided by whether a die is big enough to tap on its own, so a map at one cell per group behaves exactly as it did before grouping existed.

arguments.description: The group descriptor. See SubstrateMapGroupSelection: fixed-size, with a bins histogram truncated at ten and a remainder, and member cells fetched separately through readGroupMembers().
